title: Field seller ops lab notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, gritty notebook for field sellers and SEs to run 15–60 minute pilot discovery and canary exercises with customers. Not a polished deck — think: crumpled pocket notebook full of punchlines, short scripts, and quick diagnostic checks. Use for live roleplays and last-minute customer prep.

Audience:
- Field sellers (1: many)
- Solutions engineers running pilot onboarding
- Account engineers troubleshooting early-stage pilot failures

High-level objective:
- Convert trial usage to a paid pilot by removing two blockers: perceived latency risk and cost unpredictability.
- Give sellers 3 concrete, repeatable plays that can be executed in <30 minutes.

Quick plays (each ~10–20 mins)
1) Canary sanity + fallback demo ("Show the escape hatch")
- Slide title: Canary run & quick fallback
- Goal: Prove the app stays up with graceful degradation when capacity or model quality changes
- Steps:
  - Setup: demo app with a single route to Redwood hosted model (model-A) + fallback route to cheaper variant (model-B) via routing policy sample (show config snippet)
  - Execute: trigger a simulated high load or change traffic weight to 100% fallback for 60s
  - Show: same user flows continue, slight quality delta explained to customer, latency observed in console
- Seller script: "If we detect capacity pressure we'll shift traffic to a compatible variant — so you keep serving while we auto-heal. Quality slight drop is expected; we can pin prompts or pin model version per route."
- Quick diagnostics to collect: console screenshot (latency graph), request ids for 3 sample calls, token counts.
- Jira to log after demo: JIRA-GTM-948

2) Cost-safety demo ("Meter + cap in 5 mins")
- Slide title: Live cost guardrails
- Goal: Show predictable billing levers during pilot
- Steps:
  - Walk through per-route quota and burst cap settings in Console (show quick path)
  - Demonstrate how to set per-token or per-route daily cap (set cap low for demo)
  - Show simulated overuse and automatic throttle + notification email template
- Script: "We can enforce a hard cap for the pilot so billing surprises are removed — you'll get alerted and requests above cap will be rejected with a clear error code."
- Metrics to log: quota configured, alert email, sample error code 429+body.

3) Latency-tuned probe ("3-turn SLA check")
- Slide title: SLA probe + fallback thresholds
- Goal: Validate end-to-end tail latency for a representative request pattern
- Steps:
  - Define a 3-turn prompt set that mirrors customer load (short, medium, long)
  - Run 10 sequential probes per prompt from customer region (or use w/ Console synthetic runner)
  - Record p50/p95/p99, show warm vs cold-run differences
- Script: "We treat tail latency as a first-class metric: here’s how we measure and where we set thresholds for auto-routing to lower-latency variants."
- What to capture: p50/p95/p99, KV-cache hit-rate if available, whether batching changed p95.

Slide skeleton for a 6-slide quick deck (for SE to present):
1) One-liner + value: "Redwood: predictable inference that keeps apps online" + 2 bullets (latency, cost controls)
2) Playbook overview: three quick plays + expected outcomes (what the customer will see)
3) Canary demo (screenshots + brief runbook)
4) Cost-safety demo (console steps + cap example)
5) Latency probe (what we measure and tolerance thresholds)
6) Next steps + pilot checklist (owner, timeline, success metrics)

Common objections and scripts (rapid responses):
- Objection: "We can't risk degraded quality."
  - Script: "We isolate routes for sensitive flows and pin model versions to avoid drift. For critical paths we'll route only to high-fidelity variants and keep cheaper variants for best-effort flows."
- Objection: "Cost could balloon during demos."
  - Script: "We set hard per-route/session caps and simulate overage during this call — nothing will incur beyond the cap without explicit approval."
- Objection: "How do you measure performance in our network?"
  - Script: "We run a short synthetic probe from your region and instrument with request IDs so we can correlate traces in your observability stack."

Pilot handoff checklist (to attach to pilot run JIRA):
- Pilot owner assigned (name + email)
- Success metrics (accuracy threshold, p95 latency target, spend cap)
- Routes & model versions pinned
- Canary fallback policy configured and tested
- Notification channels configured (pager/email/slack)

Examples / quick prompts to use during demo (copyable):
- Short QA prompt: "Extract the action items from: {{doc_excerpt}}"
- Summarize prompt (multi-turn): "User: summarize the following thread in 3 bullets. Assistant:"
- Safety-check probe: "Detect policy-sensitive content in: {{sample_text}} and return yes/no and reason"

Notes to self (unresolved / TODO):
- Need a tiny GIF (6s) that demonstrates traffic shift from model-A to model-B in Console — ask design for motion spec.
- Confirm Console path for per-route caps (product doc may have moved) — linked artifact placeholder above.
- Add short troubleshooting checklist for when model-B quality gap > 20% (metric we need to define).

Post-demo follow-ups (email template snippet):
"Thanks for running the pilot with us today — attached are the screenshots and the p95 traces we captured. Next step: agree on target p95 and spend cap for a 2-week pilot. I'll open a pilot JIRA with the checklist we ran."

Roleplay prompts for seller practice (5 min warmup):
- SE plays skeptical engineer: "What happens when your GPUs fill up?" (seller must answer fallback and pin strategy)
- PO plays CFO: "Why won't this cost us X?" (seller must walk through caps and synthetic probe evidence)
- DevPS plays SRE: "How do I get logs and traces?" (show Console trace correlation and request IDs)

Appendix: quick concat of console snippets (for SE copy/paste)
- Routing policy small sample: (pseudo) "route: weight: model-A:90, model-B:10; fallback: model-B when latency>750ms"
- Quota example: "route_quota: daily_tokens: 100k; hard_cap: true; notify: team@acme.com"

Links / references used in earlier iterations:
- CONFLUENCE-5123 (pilot templates)
- JIRA-GTM-948 (pilot checklist)
- GitHub: seller-playbook/pull/72 (console snippets PR)

Final thoughts / voice notes: keep this punchy. The goal is to remove friction in the first 15 minutes of the pilot: if the buyer sees continuity (no outage), clear cost caps, and a measured p95, they generally convert to a paid pilot.

-- end of notebook --
